clue.text: Lack of bottle, but not hot dogs

parts.note: something not hot is chilly or cold
dogs is old slang for feet, as in 'my dogs are barking'

explanation.surface: A timid person's lack of nerve contrasted with a snack of hot dogs that is no longer warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, so a lack of bottle is a loss of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for losing one's nerve before acting is to get this, so it names a lack of courage.

clue.text: Maestro conducted North American guy with the goods

indicators.note: conducted suggests the letters of maestro are led or arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An orchestra's maestro leads a North American man who brings the goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maestro conducted' looks like a musical picture, but 'conducted' is the anagram signal on MAESTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers marks this as North American for a storekeeper, a person in charge of stock or a storeroom.

clue.text: "Hackney's parking area burden", I utter

parts.note: a tax is a burden or strain imposed on someone
utter and rank both mean complete or absolute, as in 'rank amateur'

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a phrase about a parking burden in Hackney, the London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: A hackney carriage is the formal British name for a licensed cab, so 'Hackney' here is not the London borough but a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: Licensed cabs, known as hackney carriages, wait for fares at a designated stand in the street.

clue.text: Leg fixed, so all ready to proceed with the show?

definitions.text: all ready to proceed with the show?

parts.note: a leg of a journey is a stage
fixed in place means set

explanation.surface: A broken leg has been mended, so the performer is fit to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase, a theatre stage that is set is prepared for the performance to begin.

clue.text: Loose-wired ring card

indicators.note: loose wiring is wiring knocked out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An electrical warning about a greeting card whose loop of wiring has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric or comical person.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a person with odd or amusing ways, which is close to an eccentric oddball.

clue.text: Wally's new trendy web domain number two

parts.note: something trendy is in fashion, or in
.com is the common commercial web domain
number two is the childish euphemism for faeces, poop

explanation.surface: Someone called Wally has a new trendy website and is second in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wally' is British slang for a fool, not a name. Its 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Fallen legend (vicar, USA) wings off

indicators.note: the wings of the phrase are its outer letters, here taken off both ends

explanation.surface: An American vicar's legendary fall, with wings that came off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings off' removes the V at the start and the A at the end of VICARUSA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he flew too close to the sun, his wax wings melted, and he fell into the sea.

clue.text: See 1
Country said to to drop right to Roman port

indicators.note: to drop tells us to remove a letter from the sounded word
said means we use how the country's name sounds when spoken

parts.note: the European country Austria

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to go from a country to the right, to a Roman port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns AUSTRIA into OSTRIA by sound, and 'to drop right' removes the R. The doubled 'to' in the printed clue is a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour city at the mouth of the Tiber, serving Rome.

clue.text: See 21
Colour transposed on double weapon

indicators.note: transposed means the letters of the colour are turned around back to front

parts.note: red is a colour
a ringer is a dead ringer, someone's double

explanation.surface: A coloured design is transposed onto a double-barrelled weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, named after its American maker Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Artist associates cobalt with moonshine

parts.note: Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt
moonshine means nonsense, as does rot

explanation.surface: A painter who mixes cobalt blue paint with illicit liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: See 23
Fancy Old Man Time

parts.note: cove is old-fashioned British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A personification: imagine Old Man Time, like Father Time.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to want it, which is to desire it greedily.

clue.text: Grants helm needs moving to be within reach

indicators.note: needs moving says the letters of the two words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grants that the ship's helm must be shifted so it can be reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at this distance is just as far as one can stretch out, so it can be reached.

clue.text: Is oxygen rejected in rocky moss's diffusion process

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
rejected means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A science question about whether oxygen is kept out as it diffuses through moss on rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses IS O to OSI, which goes 'in' OSMS, a rearrangement of MOSS ('rocky').
explanation.definitionFit: This is the passage of a solvent through a membrane, a type of diffusion studied in biology.

clue.text: Full day education reduced

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut down to its short form, keeping only its start

parts.note: the word education, shortened

explanation.surface: A busy day of schooling has been cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full after eating means being satisfied, with appetite gone.

clue.text: In love? No, mate, hate!

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A spurned partner says it is not love, it's hate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' says the answer is concealed within LOVE NO MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter spite or malice, close to hatred.

clue.text: See 23
Pure and simple, back to front man is burgeoning

indicators.note: back to front here means the last letter of the word is brought round to the front

parts.note: mere means nothing more than, pure and simple
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A plain, simple man has his back turned to the front as he grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' moves the final E of MERE to the front, giving EMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burgeoning is just coming into being or developing, like an emerging trend.

clue.text: Start a likely place for filming

definitions.meaning: the beginning of something, as of an illness
read as two words, a camera crew is on the set when shooting

explanation.surface: A film crew begins work at a suitable location.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a beginning; the second splits the word into a phrase for being at the film studio.

clue.text: Catch: girls enquire about making the impossible match

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A catch from girls who enquire about a hopeless pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for attempting the impossible comes from the old geometric problem of matching a circle's area with a square.

clue.text: Bar turning up large American rye starters, followed by Bells?

indicators.note: turning means the word for bar is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: bar means except, as does but

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A barman flips a bar stool up and serves American rye starters before the bells ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Tubular Bells is Mike Oldfield's 1973 album, so the answer is the word that comes before 'Bells'.
explanation.definitionFit: The album title Tubular Bells has this word in front, so it is the word that Bells follows.

clue.text: Packaging with definitive range that involves a complete turnaround

parts.note: packaging goods is boxing them
the is the definite article, so a definitive word
range or scope means compass, as in 'within the compass of'

explanation.surface: A packaging firm with a definitive product range that has done a full U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming all thirty-two points in order goes right round the circle, so the phrase also means a full reversal of opinion.

clue.text: It's not common for equivalence to replace power with resistance

indicators.note: to replace tells us one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: parity is equality or equivalence
P is the physics symbol for power
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A physics lesson: swap power for resistance in an equation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replace power with resistance' swaps P for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom found or uncommon is a scarce thing, a rare one.

clue.text: Set out to be Europe's premier unknown poet?

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: x is the algebraic unknown
Ezra Pound was an American poet

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to become Europe's leading unknown poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out or explain a theory in detail.

clue.text: Number 10, when backing a settler in Britain

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the combined letters are reversed

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Number 10 Downing Street, when it supports a newcomer to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' looks like the Prime Minister's residence, but it gives NO and X separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxons were Germanic people who settled in Britain in the fifth and sixth centuries.

clue.text: State's up at the end of the reserve

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state, with its 's

indicators.note: at the end of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A state is placed at the end of a reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State's' is VA plus the S, VAS, which 'up' reverses to SAV.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to keep it back for later, to put it by.

clue.text: Fancy gaiters required in upmarket transport — official

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the car

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, a luxury car

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An official in fancy gaiters must ride in a posh car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges GAITERS to EGISTRA, placed 'in' RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official who keeps records, such as of births, marriages and deaths.

clue.text: Inviting severely disheartened divorcee to enter

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside
disheartened means the heart of the word is removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: A deeply discouraged divorcee is invited to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexy is alluring or tempting, inviting interest.

clue.text: See 3
Game vetting managed by major organisation

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and arranged anew

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a major international organisation

explanation.surface: A vetting process run by a large international body.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game, French for twenty-one, in which players try to reach that total; it is also called pontoon or blackjack.

clue.text: Buddhist school said have working gas

indicators.note: said means we use how the word sounds, not its spelling

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Followers of a Buddhist school claim to have a working gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas, used in flash lamps and headlights.
